utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that late delay, little delay. Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we please have appearances, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Kyle Wood, assisted by Alma Imamovic, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my learned friends from the OTP. Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, with Nicholas Robson, appearing on behalf of General Rasim Delic. Our case manager is Ms. Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, sir. Mr. Marinkovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please stand up and make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, can you tell the Court your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. Krstan Marinkovic. I was born in the village of Crkvena, Prnjavor Municipality on the 18th of January, 1947.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What is your father's name, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Petar. Marinkovic, Petar Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And your mother's name?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Mladja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What's your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm into agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, were you working in agriculture in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, ever since I was born, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you hear the question, Mr. Marinkovic? The question was "in July 1995".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. That's right, in July 1995 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, I want to ask you some questions about July 1995 now. Where were you in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, I was in servitude, and on the 13th of June [as interpreted] I had left my home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Wood. The interpretation said "on the 13th of June," and the script says "July."

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I was going to clarify that with the witness, with Your Honour's leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, could you clarify, please, you said you were "in servitude, and on the 13th of July, I left my home." This is what the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I had been captured on the 21st of July. The 21st of July, I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Where were you captured on the 21st of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was captured in Krcevine, at Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Just for clarity's sake, the 21st of July of which year were you captured, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Why were you in Krcevine at the moment when you were captured?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was, how should I put it, a soldier of the Serb Republic, and I was taken there. The front line was there. I didn't go there of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How long had you been there, sir, before the 21st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, how long. Ever since -- since the 30th of June, and all the way until the 21st of July. I had left home on the 30th of June. I was captured on the 21st -- the 19th -- the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, you say you were taken to the front line. Who took you there, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Which police?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb Republic police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And when you got to the front line, what unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Prnjavor Light.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What exactly were your duties with the Prnjavor Light Brigade between 30 June 1995 and 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was taken to a trench. I was in a trench. That's all I know. That was my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Sir, if you could describe this trench a little bit. When you're in the trench, which way were you facing?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't quite -- well, I can tell you the way I saw it, but I should assume that I was facing more in a westerly direction. My trench was facing west, which means I was facing Podsijelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And for the record, sir, what's Podsijelovo?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, relatively speaking, it would be some sort of a mountain. That's as much as I know, or a place, Postjelevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some more questions specifically about the 21st of July now, sir. Were you in the trench on the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: 21st, all right. The evening of the 21st, we were in the trench. But on the 21st, we sort of walked around the woods, looking for a way out. I was scared to death, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask a more specific question. What time did you wake up on the 21st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime around half past 3.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And why did you wake up at half past 3.00?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Because somebody woke me and told me that we had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what did you see when you woke up, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we saw that -- well, that's what I noticed. I wasn't at the line itself. It was just this, maybe a total of about 19 days, not that I really knew about that, but the others told me that we had just been attacked. And then the shooting started, more and more shooting. And then above my trench somebody had been wounded, somebody was moaning, somebody was doing God knows what, and somebody said, "Run, run," so I ran.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, you said the shooting started. Could you tell, sir, where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, more towards my trench from Podsijelovo, in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Was the shooting coming from across your front line or where your trench was?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, but this was the nearest to me, and then it was coming from the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Was the shooting coming from what you knew to be enemy territory, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the time. Later on, I don't know. It was all sort of mixed up already. You didn't know what was what anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So going back, you said that somebody said you should run, and why is it that you decided to run?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, why? What else could I possibly have done? We were all running, so I ran too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What did you think would happen to you if you didn't run?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I think I would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: After the shooting started, sir, where did you run to?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: To the Command, our command. How shall I put it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How far from your trench was the Command?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, about not that far. Maybe 100 metres as the crow flies. But this way, perhaps 300, 400 metres. I don't know. I didn't exactly, you know ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what did you do once you got to the Command?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, I realised that everybody was running, and then I continued running from the Command towards the woods. There was a neighbour with me, Petko Maric. He had been at the Command during the time I was in the trench, and then we sort of met up. We headed through the woods this way and that, and then I was told to go home. But until the operation started, I don't think I would even have been able to go home on my own. This was the first time. I found myself in the area. I wasn't familiar with it. I didn't know which way to turn and where to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I want to ask you something to clarify things, sir. It says in the transcript that you were told to go home.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody had told me to go home when I was at the line, "Krstan, there you go, off you go, go home, no need for you to be here," funny thing, I don't think I would have been able to go home, to find my way back home, to leave the place at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Were you alone when you were running through the woods?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Petko Maric was with me, a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And in which direction did you flee when you went into the woods?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I have no idea where we fled to. If it wasn't Vozuca -- that's what was in front of us. Was it Vozuca? I don't know those places. We were just moving about the woods. We had no idea where we were going, and we bumped into a man, Tosic, Velibor, and then the three of us spent the entire day walking around the woods. And then in the evening, we sort of decided that there was no choice but to surrender and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So you said in the evening, you said, there was no choice but to surrender. Did you, in fact, surrender, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We did, we did surrender. I think it was 7.00, half past 7.00 perhaps, thereabouts. I wasn't wearing a watch. Well, I was, but it was seized. But I assume that it could have been sometime about half past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Where were you when you decided to surrender?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We were moving about the woods. I don't know where. We had just reached Krcevine, just past the Command -- where our Command used to be, and then from the woods we had a view of the command post, and there were soldiers milling about there, coming and going, on horseback, horses, carrying goods, and we were just observing this, thinking, "What shall we do?" I wasn't really optimistic about our surrender, but it just happened that way. The other two -- Petko actually was saying, "Let's surrender," and I said, "No, I don't think so. If we surrender, we'll be tortured and killed just the same." We'd be better off -- I wasn't carrying anything. I used to have a rifle, but I lost it somewhere along the way. I had stumbled on a tree stump, and I had a grenade. I decided to kill myself, but Petko said, "No," and then Tosic said, "Krle, whatever you think is best," which means that he had already agreed. But Petko was adamant we should surrender, "We shall survive." And then it was touch and go, should we surrender, should we not surrender. We were right there in the middle of the woods. All it took was a step forward into the field. As soon as we were out in the field, they would have seen us. "Shall we not tug-of-war?" We walked out. They ran in our direction immediately, and we immediately put our hands up in the air above our heads and walked in their direction. They encircled us, started hitting us and kicking us and that sort of thing down where our Command used to be. And then they told us to lie down on the ground, hands on our backs. They tied our hands. They beat us and kicked us. It was all full of dust, vehicles, light vehicles passing by, I kept my head down to keep my head from all the dust, and then a soldier came down and took my head and stuck it in the dirt. That's the way it had to be, and then two Mujahedin and one Bosnian were told to take us away. Can I tell -- do you mind if I tell you about this, what exactly happened after we'd surrendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, I do plan to ask you about that, sir, but I want to ask you a few questions about something you've already said. You said that you were encircled as soon as you stepped out of the forest. Could you determine who it was who encircled you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I said we came out of the woods and they were near our Command. They ran in our direction. We walked in their direction, and then they encircled us and started hitting us immediately down near our Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And when you say "they," sir, who do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean those who captured us. That's who I mean. The Bosnian Muslims and the Mujahedin, that's who I mean. I can't possibly mean my own, can I?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And when you say "the Bosnian Muslims and the Mujahedin," could you describe, sir, how you could tell the difference between the Bosnian Muslims and the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the difference is neat. Those people were black and those people were more blue. I never saw any black Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, the transcript says "those people were more blue." Is that what you said? And if so, what do you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The transcript says "Those people were more black and those people were more blue."

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the distinction, the way I see it. You could say white, then black. I'm not sure how I could possibly explain this. I don't think I'm able to explain it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could you tell, sir, what was the proportion of people you deemed to be Mujahedin versus those you thought to be Bosnian Muslims in the group that had surrounded you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the proportion might be 50/50 there. I didn't exactly count them, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: When these soldiers surrounded you and took you prisoner, could you hear what they were saying?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were swearing at us, mentioning our Chetnik mothers, "We will kill you all," and, well, just after I'd headed out, the loudspeakers at the Muslims, they were using loudspeakers and they told us to surrender, so maybe that prompted us to do just that, hoping that we would be exchanged for the Srebrenica people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could you hear what the Mujahedin were saying?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we could, but we didn't understand. I didn't understand -- understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: During the process of your surrender, sir, did you sustain any injuries?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I received a blow by a rifle-butt right here [indicates]. I still have a mark. My lip was split, and something on my head -- somebody cracked me over the head with a rifle, the tip of the rifle, and then somebody perhaps didn't like them to hit me like that, but somebody just went ahead and did it anyway. Well, this is merely an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: For the record, I'd like the record to reflect that when the witness said he was hit "right here," he held his right hand to the back of his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we establish what the assumption is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, you said in your testimony that -- you spoke of an assumption, your assumption. Could you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that somebody wouldn't let them hit me, and then somebody hit me over somebody else, and that's why I got hit by the tip of the rifle barrel. That's the assumption. If it had been an open blow, no, but they had to actually lean over somebody else to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown, well, it's Exhibit P06072. I believe we can call that up in Sanction. And for the record, this is a video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood, P06?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, P06072. That is ERN V005672

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, do you recognise the people depicted in that video?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Krstan Marinkovic. That's me. Petko Maric and Velibor Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And for the record, at the end there, there were the three people standing in a row. Which one of those was you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The middle one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And which was the person to the right, as you're looking at the screen?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Petko Maric, Petko.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could you describe for the record what Petko Maric was wearing when you saw him in the video?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: What he was wearing? Wearing. What exactly do you mean? The sweater and olive-grey trousers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're conducting this exercise, I'm wondering if it might be possible to get the video back up on screen and pause it so we can see who we're talking about. It's just a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was going to ask the same, but I thought Mr. Wood wanted to do something before the witness sees the thing again. Would you like to consider that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, that's an excellent suggestion. I see that it's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, do you see that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: So there are three men. You identified yourself as the person in the middle. Petko Maric is the person --

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the right from where I'm standing, like this, Tosic, the one behind me on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And for the record, what he's looking at now is at time code two minutes 30 seconds point four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, when this video might have been taken?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be sure, but I assume it was that day, the day we were captured, but I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, where were you taken after you were captured?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: They took us from Krcevine towards Podsijelovo, to a place called Livade, but I don't know these places. All I heard was that we were in Livade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How long did it to take you to get to the place that you know as Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that we walked for an hour or an hour and a half. We couldn't go then. We stopped a bit. They were sitting and we were standing. Then we would start moving again and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Do you know about how far it is you walked from Krcevine to Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was about four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Who was with you when you were being taken to Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: There were two Mujahedin and one Bosnian. Each one had his own. Actually, the one next to me was the Bosnian, and then these two Mujahedin. I know we came up to a kind of little canal, and it was nice, clean water and we were thirsty, so the man who was next to me, he said, "Well, if it were up to me, I would let you, but I really don't dare because of the others."

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what do you believe he meant by, "but I really don't dare because of the others"?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I really wouldn't know why he said that, why he was afraid of them enough not to let us drink water. I mean, I can't -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you see any other soldiers between Krcevine and Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then we went towards Livade. We were intercepted by Bosnians, Mujahedin. A man passed by on a motorcycle, a Mujahedin, very strong-built, large man. He got off the motorbike. Petko was in front, then Tosic, then me. Then he hit or punched Petko, then Tosic, then myself. And the punch was so strong that I ran across the road, and then I was hit by a soldier with a butt of his rifle, and that's where I got a cut lip. Then we were beaten by all of them. It's a long story, but by the time we reached Livade, we were beaten a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: You said you were beaten by all of them. Do you mean both the person who came and the people who were escorting you and the other two?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not the ones who were escorting us. They didn't beat us. I assume that their Command was somewhere in Livade and they were moving around. There were constantly vehicles, cars passing. There were civilians. We encountered a large group of soldiers, civilians, women. "The Chetniks are coming." This Bosnian said, "Mother, the Chetniks are here." This woman was holding a pitchfork, taking hay to the cows, and she began with the pitchfork, and we thought, well, now we are done for. But then she plunged them into the ground, and then she took a pole used to hold up bean shoots, and then she started beating us with that, saying, "You killed my son." And then this Bosnian moved to get us away, but then we encountered even worse evil as we continued. We were encountered by women, civilians, soldiers, as we were going towards Livade, close to that house. And then I was hit -- I had to go under the wire. I was asked to come up. I couldn't do it. Somebody pulled me out. Somebody jumped on me, and some grandmother said, "Children, don't, Allah sees it." And then somebody grabbed me and took me to this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, where was this house that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, it was in Livade. I don't know more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And the people escorting you, what did they do when these other people were beating you and mistreating you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: They stopped us, but then later I could see that preparations were being made. The soldier from the Command, a Bosnian, told me to bend down more, more, more. He was holding a child by the arm. The child was about 10 or 11 years old. He was wearing a multicoloured uniform and military shoes. And then the child really broke my nose. There was blood all over my face. But the Bosnian kept saying to him,"Faster, faster, faster," so that this boy would get it all out on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: You said earlier in your testimony that you were taken to the house. Who took you to the house?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Those three that were escorting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And was there anybody in the house when you got there?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Velibor Trivicevic, Branko Cucic and Samac. There were four of them. Then the two of us, there was six, and then by the end of the night there were a total of 12 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Were there any enemy soldiers in the house?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a Mujahedin at the entry door to the house, and he would punch everybody once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague has just drawn to my attention a potential translation error. I'm referring to page 15, line number 23. In the transcript, it states "but the Bosnian kept saying to him, 'Faster, faster, faster,' so that this boy would get it all out on me." Mrs. Vidovic understands that the Bosnian was speaking to the witness when he was saying, "Faster, faster, faster." So I wonder if this matter could be clarified, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, if you could explain, please, the Bosnian who kept saying, "Faster, faster, faster," --

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. While the boy was getting ready to hit me, I was bending down. And then when the child hit me, then I raised my head. And then the Bosnian said, "Faster, faster, faster," that we should get out of there because there was a crowd of soldiers, people, children, grandmothers, grandfathers. All of them were saying, "Where are the Chetniks?" They were all saying, "Killed my son," and so on. He told me -- he told us because he wanted to get us out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. When you got to the house, where were you -- where were you placed within the house?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: A room. There was a room. There were a few entrance stairs, a veranda, a corridor, and then a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Were you detained in that room, restrained in any way?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. When we got there, a Mujahedin tied our feet and hands. I had a sweater that I was wearing, and he placed it over like this [indicates], and some -- he bound some of their eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How long did you remain in this room in the house, Mr. Marinkovic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there that night and then the following day. We got there in the evening, and then the next day, and then the day after we left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you remain restrained in this way the entire time you were in Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said that that night, the next day, then a night, and then the second day -- I don't know how that would be, the second day after or the third day. Well, I don't know. I'm going to put it like this and then you can see how you understand it. We arrived that evening, then the day, then another night, and then that was -- yeah, the second or the third day that we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you sustain any injuries as a result of your time in Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We had scars from the wire and so on, and there was bleeding in some places.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you have contact with the enemy soldiers when you were in Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came to us, cursed us, insulted us, "We're going to kill you," we'll do this, we'll do that. Some women also came. We had our eyes bound. They told us, "You killed my son." She hit us with something, struck us. Everyone hit us. Somebody kicked us. They used their feet. Some used sticks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Were you given any food or water when you were in Livade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. Yes, someone asked, but we didn't get anything. I didn't get anything. I don't know about the others. They asked if we would eat "burek." I mean, I hardly think that, but, anyway, I didn't get anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: You said you stayed in Livade a few days. Where were you taken after that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We were taken, but we don't know. They came, they untied our legs. Our hands were still tied. We still had blinds. And we were taken, I assume, to something that was a truck. It was difficult to climb up. Our hands were tied. Then we were just thrown into the truck, and we went like that. It was a longer trip. They stopped by somewhere. Maybe it was on the lines of the army. You could hear a lot. They said all sorts of things to us. They took us off the truck at one point. I tried to wriggle out. I couldn't. Then I fell, and then I assume that it was a machine-gun, an 84 or a 53, next to my head. Some shots were fired, and I was strewn with earth, and then again we were thrown back into the truck. And then we came to Gostovici. I guess we got there maybe at 10.00 -- well, if we left Livade at 10.00 or 11.00, we could have been up there maybe at noon or 3.00 or 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what happened immediately when you got to Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened was that we were sitting somewhere that was a road, at the edge of the road. Our blinds were taken off, and we sat down. And there was some cars, there was some insignia of the Red Cross. And then we were thinking, well, it's a good thing we're going to the Red Cross then. And then the Mujahedin and the Bosnians gathered around. There were all kinds of curses, insults, and we were sitting there. A Mujahedin came and he was walking among us. He had two knives, and he was sharpening one against the other. He was doing something like rolling up his sleeves, and this had the effect on me that he knelt, he rolled his sleeves up. I was sitting, and I know that he pulled me to the left side by my hair, and he kneeled down and placed a knife on my neck. And then they were talking, saying something. The Bosnian came up and took that knife from his hand and said, "Doctor." And then the Mujahedin said, "Doctor, Doctor." And then Sikanic, Branko Sikanic, called back. That was him. He was the doctor. He was captured with us. He responded, and then that Mujahedin went up to him. The Bosnian gave Branko the knife, that Branko should cut my throat and if he did not cut my throat, he would cut his throat. And Branko refused that. He said, "Sir, I was taught to help people. I cannot do that." And then he gave the knife to the Mujahedin, and then in the same way that he bent me to the side, I was able to look a little bit. And that's what happened to him, to Branko. He was in the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If I could ask you something, sir. You said in your statement here "he was captured with us," and I wonder if you could clarify. You're referring to Branko Sikanic, and in the video we saw --

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: -- the three of you that had been captured. At what point did you see the doctor, Branko Sikanic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that the three of us were captured, Petko, Tosic and myself, in Krcevine. We found this guy, Sikanic, Trivicevic, Cucic and Samac in Livade. They had been captured before, and then we came to Livade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I apologise for interjecting again. It's the same matter as last time, a potential translation error. My colleague, in listening to the witness, understood that in relating about what happened involving this knife, that nothing happened during the incident, so Mrs. Vidovic's understanding is that the witness used words to the effect that nothing happened, and that is not reflected in the transcript. So I wonder if perhaps this matter could please be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, were you cut with a knife during this incident?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Was Dr. Sikanic cut with a knife during this incident?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What happened after this incident in which you were -- the knife was held to your throat?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He went away. Sikanic also. I think it was just intimidation. Nothing happened, but I didn't know that it would go like that, will it happen -- would it happen, would it not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Where exactly were you when this happened, sir? You said you'd been taken off the truck. Were you outside or inside?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Outside. I said that there was a road and we were sitting on the curb. Some were sitting here. They were walking between us or among us, talking, speaking insults.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: When you say "they," who do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I am thinking of the Mujahedin and the Bosnians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Do you understand what some of the people were saying, some of the enemy soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard the Bosnians. Of course we understood them. They cursed our mothers, "Your throats will be cut," this will happen, that will happen, insults.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How long were you in that position after being taken off the truck?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We were like that for about two hours, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And where were you taken after that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: To a house, a house that was all hit by shells. It was demolished. There was nothing inside. Everything inside was burned. We were brought to a room, and they put some blankets down, and that's where we were that night. In the morning, you could hear something banging in the other room. They placed a floor there and they boarded the windows up, and then they moved us to that room which was right next-door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: You say the house was demolished, sir. Could you describe specifically what the house looked like?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The house looked knocked down. There was no roof. There were only a couple of chimneys standing. There was no door -- there were no door frames or window frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, you're being handed some photographs. I'd like you to take a look at those, and perhaps we can put those on ELMO. And while you do, the Prosecution would like to tender that clip from P06072, Your Honour. That would be from time code 00.01.52.5 to 00.02.39.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem I have with that clip, sir, is that it's not marked who's who on that, and this witness testified about those people on the clip. You didn't even get him to say who's who on that, to write down who's who. Or are you going to be able later to identify those people?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Well, he did make the record, Your Honour, of where they were standing in relation to himself. Let me check just one moment. We could, Your Honour, time permitting, bring up a still for him to write on the photograph to make it absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, you can do that later. P06072 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 540.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, looking at those photos, do you recognise the house in which you were held in Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recognize anything here. It looks like the one with the two chimneys, but how can I tell now? But at the time, it was knocked down, with only the two chimneys standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Sir, there are a few photographs there. Are you speaking of each of the photographs or just the one that's showing on the ELMO right now?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I am looking at the one in front of me. I mean, it has the appearance. I don't know if it looked like this or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could look at the other photographs as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Same case. That's what it looked like. There are the two chimneys again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And, sir, I wonder if you could -- if you could be given a pen and write -- circle the house which you're referring to with the two chimneys.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you could look at the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The same thing, the same case. The two chimneys, but I cannot recognise anything else other than the two chimneys. I knew that there was no roof, but how can I tell now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And could you again, sir, circle the building you're referring to with the two chimneys?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I could have those two photographs admitted into evidence, Your Honour, the two on which he made marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I oppose the admission of the photographs. We've heard from the witness in respect of all three of the photographs and also in respect to two that he circled the chimneys, that he cannot recognise them, so we would submit that there is no probative value to these photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Your Honour, he did indicate that this is a house that looked like the house that he could have been in. I believe that is sufficient for these to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Wood, who took the photographs and who took the video that we admitted just a while ago? Where do these exhibits come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at the risk of having to testify, to lay the foundation for this, I can tell you that these photos are on our exhibit list, that from the previous video that was entered into evidence, P06072, I believe that was taken from ABH Archive. And as to this video, the video from which this particular still is taken, I don't have that information at my fingertips, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to make the Defence's position clear, Your Honour, in respect of the second video, the latter video just mentioned by my learned friend from which these photographs were produced, the Defence do contest the authenticity of elements of that video, so we're certainly not accepting where these photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you telling us that these photographs come from a video, because I am not aware of that. You are putting that on the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, these are from a video, and for the record that is P06032 on the Prosecution's exhibit list. This is an instance, Your Honour, where I believe we will have more testimony as to this exhibit from witnesses later on, and that's really all I have to say about this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are you suggesting now? Are you suggesting to mark them for identification, to mark it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I believe that's an excellent suggestion, Your Honour, that we have these marked for identification and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are going to call a witness who can identify it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's the Prosecution's plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The photos are admitted into evidence to be marked for identification. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these photos will be Exhibit Number 541 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, with whom were you placed into that room in the house that we were just speaking about?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We were all there, all 12 of us, at Livade. We were all assembled there. There were 12 of us in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: For the record, could you please say the names of those 12 people -- actually, the 11 other people?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting -- sorry, if I may interrupt. I'm not sure whether I'm getting lost. Are we still in Livade or are we in Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think as the transcript indicates, he's indicated they were taken to Gostovici, thrown off the truck. He describes the incident with the knives and then the house in which they were at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then you say, page 26, line 9, says: "We were all there, all 12 of us, at Livade." I'm not sure now where we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll clarify that with him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, with whom were you transported from Livade to Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: All 12 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what were the -- what were the names of the 11 other people with whom you were transferred?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Without me, you mean? All right. Branko Sikanic, Tosic, Velibor, Trivicevic, Velibor, Samac, Miodrag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I can remember all of them now. Should I start all over?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do, sir. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has what appears to be a notebook in front of him, and he's lifted it up. I don't know if there's anything written on there or not, but I just thought I better alert the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Marinkovic -- Mr. Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Look at me. What do you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some sort of a notebook, free for all to have a look, if you like, but I don't have all the names. I'll just try to do it like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, do try to do it like that, Mr. Marinkovic. The procedure in this forum is that you don't look at notes unless you are given notes to look at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing, nothing at all. Fine. Sikanic, Branko. Velibor Trivicevic, Velibor Tosic, Petko Maric, Vlado Cucic, Dusko Pejicic -- how many so far? Gojko Vujicic. How many so far?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Seven. Eight, with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not an exam. If you don't remember, don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult to remember all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's perfectly understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If I could ask you, sir, of those you mentioned, you mentioned someone named Gojko Vujicic. Do you recall what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember all too well. But you know something? Were you to ask me about the date now, the exact day, well, I know it was when we reached --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the first or the second night we were there. The old woman then took us to the cellar, and then that night --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, I need to interrupt you just for a moment here. I need to make sure that the record is clear. You say you don't remember the exact day, but you said, "I know it was when we reached ...," and then the interpreter didn't catch your answer.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the day before, the day after? I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The day before what or the day after what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Let me ask, then: You're describing something that's going on with Mr. Vujicic. If you could just be clear, where exactly did this happen?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: At Gostovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And if you could please continue your answer of what happened to Gojko Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This was the second or third evening there, the second let's say. Someone came over that evening, a Bosnian man. Gojko was standing next to the door. He untied his legs, and then a Mujahedin brought something in a bowl, some fish and bread. He cut his restraint loose. He fed each of us a morsel of bread and a little fish. We tried to chew and swallow to the extent that we could. And then he brought us a litre of water and fed each of us some water. Those were his orders. We were there, and then 15 or 20 minutes later, and I think it was sometime around half past 8.00 -- it was dark by this time. This was some sort of dinner for us, I suppose. But then someone came over, freed our hands and feet. Was it that house, the playground behind? I'm not really sure, but we were nearby. And then somehow I was thrown to the ground. I ended up lying face down on the ground, and most probably the rest of us, too. And then someone came over and tied our feet up again. I'm not sure what they used, but it felt like some sort of a hose. They tied our feet up, and we were all moaning. There was a Bosnian man there, and he said, "Stay still." He mentioned my mother, and he said, "I'll finish you, I'll beat you with a pole." And then the -- the restraint round my feet sort of started loosening, and it went on like that throughout the night. I didn't really see that, because I was all tied up, but this man was standing near me, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: When the restraint was tight, sir, how did that feel?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: That he would cut my feet off. It was so tight -- the restraint was so tight that I thought my feet would just fall off. So Gojko was moaning, and we were all lying down. We all wanted water. Some of us had fever, and, "Water, water." And then the Bosnian said, "Want some water," I said, "Sure," and he brought a bottle and he put it in my mouth, and I realised it was urine so I turned my head away and then he spilled it all over my face, and that kind of thing. When we were still on the ground and Gojko was moaning, and he said, "Bring us some water. I am parched, and these people are killing me. I can't hold out anymore." And then he cursed at him, "But bring me some water, because I can't do this anymore." It was nighttime. I heard a rifle shot near me, but I had no idea what was happening. So it was like that throughout the night, and then the next morning -- the next morning -- well, morning or night, but someone came up to me and helped me to turn around and sit up, and then someone took my blindfold off and put Gojko's head in my lap. I flinched. They pulled him by the hair and pulled his head up level with mine, and they said, "Kiss your brother." This was the Mujahedin. And then they took us away, this way and that. Someone struck me right here [indicates]. I was bleeding. I was thinking everyone else has been killed already, now it's my turn. So they were taking me there, and when we got near the house, I realised everybody was there but Gojko. And then later on the Mujahedin came --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question, sir? When you say, "Someone struck me here," and you indicated, where did you indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two men taking me away, held me by the arm, and I couldn't walk on my own because my legs had been bound throughout the whole the previous night, so they were numb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is: Where were you struck on your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they turned me around, they threw my head, kissed my head, and then I was pulled up. And then they took me to the house, where we were. And near the house, someone struck me, and the other two were holding me back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Where on your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At my temple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, on your temple. Thank you so much. You may proceed, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I see it's almost time for the break. I do have maybe one or two more questions, and then maybe that would be the appropriate time, with Your Honour's leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, if you could please -- could you describe what condition Gojko Vujicic's head was in when it was shown to you in the morning?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Gojko's head, I know Gojko head cut off, stuff dangling loose, head all blue, dead man's head. What should I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you notice if there were any wounds on the head, for example?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we did see that in the room, not right then. When I was brought to the room, then later the Mujahedin came, and there was some sort of hook, the head like that, and they put it on the wall. So the six of us were there next to the wall, five over there [indicates], and then this wall facing us [indicates], the head dangling with a gunshot wound to the temple.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness was indicating with his right hand to his right temple. That is an appropriate time for a break, Your Honour. I have maybe 15 -- 10, 15 minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Just one question by me before we go. Just so that we are absolutely clear, sir, you say the head was put before you. Where was the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How should I know? Never saw the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it was the head without the body? The head was not attached to its body; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw the body. They just dropped the head in my lap. I had blood on my jeans still when I came home six months later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, before the break you were talking about this place you were kept in. You had been referring to it as "Gostovici." How did you come to know that this was the place called Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we talked among ourselves. Some people knew, I guess. I didn't. I don't know. I still believe that the place was Gostovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Who exactly was guarding you when you were at Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Mujahedin standing at the door with an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And when you say "Mujahedin," could you describe this person, what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't. A soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers at Gostovici who were not Mujahedin or who you did not perceive to be Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And how often would you see those other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not that often, but they did come around, and we heard them saying, at the door, "Let me go in and show them." And then he mentioned our Chetnik mother. To the right of the entrance to the house, there's some sort of pantry there and bathroom. Probably there was a tool shed, too. And we heard some noise from there. I think they were getting some tools, some implements, and then a Bosnian walked in with a hoe, a spade, or something. He came in. We kept our heads down, hands on knees, and he poked everybody in the chest and then whacked everybody over the spine, over the back. But he hit me on the head, too. He caught my head. I had a cut, a wound. A piece of my skin and hair on it came apart, so I still have a scar there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with any of these -- these men whose language you understood?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't dare. They were going in and out all the time, telling us all sorts of things, but we weren't supposed to answer back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How long did you remain in this place called Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We remained until the 24th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And what happened on the 24th of August that ended your stay at Gostovici?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of August, we were taken away in those chains, in a single chain, the 11 of us. The Bosnian had brought some sort of a chain. It was nighttime, but I heard his voice. He wasn't saying much. They were just mumbling among themselves. They chained our feet and locked our feet, put a bolt on it. It was an empty chain, and then all the way to the other side, the six of us, and the five of them over there, and then linking the five of them. And then some more length of chain all the way to the door. And then the 24th, when they took us away, when they took us out to wash every day, the same chain, we walked in line. And then if one misstepped, he would pull everybody else along, and then there was a lot of jerking and shaking. So we sat with our backs turned to the wall of that house over there. We were just sitting there. I don't know what this is about, but the Mujahedin came, and it was probably the Bosnian who told us -- Tosic, this Tosic, he was a small man, a rather small man, and he stammered a lot, and they asked him all sorts of questions because they were laughing at him all the time, said, "You bark like a dog, what do you mean a dog," and we all remained silent because we --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I want to interrupt you. I just want to make sure I'm clear here. When you're describing this incident with Tosic, is this on the 24th that this happened?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And were any other of the POWs treated similarly to Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I was about to say. They started with him, barking like a dog, and then he would come out, hit each and every one of us, and made us all bark like dogs, but not just like dogs. We were made to imitate the sounds of all sorts of animals; horses, swine, pigs. We had no choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: How soon after this were you taken away from the Gostovici camp?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed for a couple of hours, and then someone came over and blindfolded us. And then they came and brought chains and locks. That was the day we left, the same day. And then walked up to me and said -- the Bosnian did, no key to my lock. And then they used the hammer to break the lock on my foot. And then behind us, one by one, they took them away, and then we came -- well, most probably it was a bus, and said, "Raise your foot, there's a step, mind the step," and then we just headed for Zenica. And then we came in, they threw us in. We were falling over each other. They were hitting people, the Mujahedin, the Bosnians, what do I know, they hit everybody over their backs with a rifle-butt, and they threw us in the bus. And then we were off and got somewhere, and then the Bosnian walked onto the bus and said, "Good grace, we finally reached free territory, lads. You all have one, two, three, four German mark each. Let's have some coffee." How should we have any money on us that they taken everything away from us previously, and "When we come to a certain place and I say heads down, you just keep your heads down," so that's my assumption. If we were driving past the Mujahedin, we were supposed to keep down, and if not, meaning he allowed us to remain in our seat. And so we were off somewhere. I had no idea where we were being taken to. Maybe to be exchanged, I said. And then we realised, once we'd reached Zenica, we got to this place, they made us face the wall, they took our blindfolds off one after the other, and then we went to the correctional and penal institute. I think it was the KP Dom. Lined up against the wall, and then one by one we walked straight in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The people who were on the van and driving you, could you understand what they were saying? That is, could you understand their language?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were Bosnians, weren't they? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown P02436, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Do you see that document on the screen, Mr. Marinkovic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do, but I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Is the type too small? Perhaps if we can zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Zoom in, yes. I still can't see. Well, all right. Actually, that might -- right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, do you see the names written on that document?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I want to make sure we're looking at the same document. Do you see numbers 1 through 11 written on this document?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And can you see, after each numeral, there's a name? Can you read those names?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Maybe I should try and put my glasses on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: What do those names mean to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course they do. Of course they do. These are people who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: People who were with you at what time, Mr. Marinkovic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: From the day we were captured to the day we left captivity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Do you see the name of "Gojko Vujicic" on this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: If I could have this tendered into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Please continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said you can't see, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What can't you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see Gojko's name there. He was number 12, and as far as I can tell, there are only 11 names here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are tendering the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 542.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P02508.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I see the document, but I can't see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could zoom in a little bit on the numeral "1" on the first page of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. -- Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, does that help? Are you able to see more of that document?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I see that it's appearing larger on the screen now. Can you read it at this point, Mr. Marinkovic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Can you please read, sir, the names that follow 1, 2 and 3 on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. Guljevatej, Igor, and Stokanovic, Goran. Sikanic, Branko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm getting interpretation which is not English, and I am on Channel 4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Is Your Honour receiving the English interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I'm receiving the English interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And, Mr. Marinkovic, can you see what's next to the -- the name written next to the black dot near the bottom of the page as it appears on your screen? I think you read number 3, Sikanic, Branko. What's the next name?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: "Krstan Marinkovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And again, sir, what do these names mean to you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: These are the people who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I would ask to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 543.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, I think we can come back to the video still, Your Honour. You wished that perhaps it be marked a little bit better for the record. I do have a still from that video that can be handed to the witness, and he can make proper marks on it to make a more clear record. And for the record, this still is at time code 00.02.30.4 from video P06072 which has been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marinkovic, if I could have you turn to the actual document that's been placed on the ELMO. It's just to your right there. And I see that you have a pen in your hand. Can you please put a "1" next to the one that you identified earlier as Tosic.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is Tosic [indicates]. Where should I write? [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if there's room, could you please write that person's name next to where he's standing?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And the next person standing next to the person you've identified as Mr. Tosic, can you write the name of that person in the same relative position?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And could you please do the same for the third person shown in this video still, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if this could be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for consistency's sake, could you write a "2" next to the person in the center and "3" next to the person on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 544.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Wood. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Marinkovic. My name is Nicholas Robson.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll be asking you some questions today on behalf of General Delic. Now, Mr. Marinkovic, over the years you've made several statements relating to the events following your capture at Krcevine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've made a statement to an Investigative Judge at Prnjavor Lower Court; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a statement was given, but I cannot really remember it well. But if there is something, I will -- I will remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've also made several statements to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of this International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I only know of one, and that's this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, in your evidence, you told us that since the 30th of June, 1995, you were a member of the Prnjavor Light Brigade. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, that you were a soldier before that time? You actually served in the local defence at Potocani from September 1991?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You explained to the Trial Chamber what happened to you on the 21st of July, 1995, and how you and two other men ran away from your trench and eventually you surrendered to a group of men. You remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to refer you to is one of the statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution, dated the 12th of December, 1999. I am able to show it to you, if you would like to see the document. But if I could just, at this stage, remind you of what you said. You told the investigator that on the 21st of July: "I was captured in a battle by Mujahedin soldiers." Do you remember telling the investigator that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This question is quite unclear to me now. I was captured, and I said that, and I stand by that, that I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. The point that I want to make is that the people who captured you, you would agree with me that they were Mujahedin soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I said how we were escorted by two Bosnians and one Mujahedin, so we were captured by Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify that with you, Mr. Marinkovic, when you are referring to the Bosnians who were with the Mujahedin that captured you, these were local Bosnian men who were also people who were Mujahedins; they had similarities to Mujahedins and they were clearly with the foreign Mujahedin men?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This question is not clear to me. The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try and clarify it with you a little more. You've told us that you gave a statement to an Investigative Judge, although you can't recall very well what you said to that Judge. But if I could refer you to part of that statement, what you told the Investigative Judge was: "During capture, I spotted that Mujahedin were also present there, along with the Muslim soldiers."

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: "There were more Mujahedin than Muslim soldiers who were also called the Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I said half, half. I didn't say if there were more of the ones than the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. I accept what you're saying, the proportion was half-half, but the point that I'm trying to make is: During the statement that you gave to the Investigative Judge, you referred to the Muslim soldiers, and you said that those Muslim soldiers were also called the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Incorrect. I never said that they were called Mujahedin. These were Mujahedin, that was the Mujahedin, and the others I called "Bosnians." I don't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we can put it on the screen. It's Defence document D449, and it's page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S that I'm interested in. And in the B/C/S version, it's about halfway down the page. It's the third paragraph. Similarly, in the English it's the third paragraph as well. Mr. Marinkovic, do you see the paragraph that begins with: "During capture, I spotted that Mujahedin were also present there"?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that here or there? I don't see -- I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we're looking for a paragraph that begins: "During capture, I spotted that Mujahedin were also present there ..."

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I see it, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You can -- could you read out the first two sentences of that paragraph for us, please?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: "During capture, I spotted that Mujahedin were also present there, along with the Muslim soldiers. There were more Mujahedin than Muslims." Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No. If you can carry on reading, please, the next bit.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: "There were Mujahedin than Muslim soldiers, who were also carrying -- wearing or carrying Mujahedin. After capture, tied with our hands behind our backs --"

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, could you please read that second sentence out again, please?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The second one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: "Besides the Mujahedin, there were also Muslim soldiers. There were more Mujahedin than the Muslims, who were also called the Mujahedin --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter does not understand what the witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Let me just read back what you've just told us.

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So according to what you told the Investigative Judge back in 1997, you said: "There were more Mujahedin than Muslim soldiers, who were also called the Mujahedin." Do you agree with me that that is what your statement says?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say that. I don't agree. Perhaps it is there, but I didn't say it. That there were more there and that they were carrying insignia, I didn't say that. That's something in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. What about the part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness is saying he didn't say they were carrying insignia. I don't think there's "insignia" on the sentence. Maybe that's why there's a cross-purpose between the two of you. If you can just clear that, unless there is an insignia mentioned which I am not seeing in that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Marinkovic, would you agree with me that what you've read out to the Tribunal, to the Court a moment ago, mentions nothing about insignia?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. What insignia? They didn't have any insignia. That the Bosnians had insignia, I didn't say that. I didn't see that. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. You don't recall the Bosnians had any insignia. Let me go back to my question. What I'm interested in, in this sentence, is what you told the Investigative Judge where, when you referred to the Muslim soldiers, you said they were also called the Mujahedin. Can you explain to us what you meant when you told the Investigative Judge that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTAN MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that. It's incorrect. I don't recall that at all. I was not -- I couldn't -- I don't know if they were carrying anything in particular. I didn't see that, really. Something was done, I didn't say that. I would see it with them. I was with the people -- the Mujahedin and the Bosnians. I would have seen some insignia similar to that. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Right, yes. I understand, okay. Let me rephrase it a different way.
